content: Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that is prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as red, irritated, itchy, and watery eyes, sneezing, and a runny nose caused by hay fever, allergies, or the common cold. It is also effective in relieving itching associated with insect bites, sunburns, bee stings, poison ivy, poison oak, and minor skin irritations. Additionally, it is used to prevent and treat motion sickness, induce sleep, manage symptoms of Parkinson's disease, and relieve cough caused by minor throat or airway irritation. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Diphenhydramine is available in tablet, capsule, and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken three or four times daily. For motion sickness, it should be taken 30 minutes before travel and, if necessary, before meals and at bedtime. When used as a sleep aid, it is taken at bedtime. Always follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. Do not administer this medication to children under 6 years of age unless specifically instructed by a doctor. Before taking diphenhydramine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially those for colds, hay fever, allergies, depression, seizures, muscle relaxation, pain relief, sedation, or sleep, as well as any vitamins. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking diphenhydramine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the sedative effects of this drug, so it should be avoided. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Diphenhydramine may cause side effects. Common minor side effects include dry mouth, nose, and throat; drowsiness; upset stomach; chest congestion; and headache. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, which require immediate medical attention, include vision problems, difficulty urinating, muscle weakness, unusual excitement (especially in children), and nervousness. If you experience a severe side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store diphenhydramine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical appointments while taking this medication. Do not share it with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Diphenhydramine is marketed under various brand names, including AllerMax®, Benadryl®, Compoz®, Diphenhist®, Excedrin PM®, Nytol®, Simply Sleep®, Sleepinal®, Sominex®, and Unisom®, among others. It is also available in combination products with other active ingredients, such as acetaminophen, pseudoephedrine, or aspirin, under brand names like Alka-Seltzer PM®, Bayer PM®, Tylenol PM®, and Sudafed Sinus Nighttime Plus Pain Relief®.
